results.title: Beam at 13 Days: Reflection's 501B Bet Tested [2026]
results.content:
Sequoia Capital partner Stephanie Zhan, whose firm has backed Reflection, described Beam on social media as “a highly efficient agentic open model with 501B total parameters and 23B active,” a characterization that lines up with the active-parameter math Reflection published (source). Venture backing doesn’t settle the technical question, but it does signal that at least one serious AI-focused investor is willing to put a name behind the efficiency framing in public.

## The GLM-5.2 Benchmark Claim and Its Unconfirmed Status [...] Reflection’s central claim is that Beam uses three to four times less inference compute than rival Western open models while reasoning at a similar level. The company said it used high-compute reinforcement learning to push Beam toward efficient reasoning, cutting token cost and inference time for coding and agentic tasks without giving up much on quality. That framing matters because inference cost, not training cost, is what most companies actually pay for once a model ships. A lab can spend months training a giant model, but if every production query burns expensive GPU time, the economics fall apart fast.
